beats.role_note: COLD OPEN -- required fellow intro line + AI-voice disclosure; ask lands answered
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Boopesh M., and this video is about what the Humanitarians AI fellows taught this week, November first to the seventh. A quick note: this is an AI voice reading my script. Every number comes from the git history, counted by a small script.

props.command: What did the Humanitarians AI fellows teach in their new work folders from Nov 1 to Nov 7?
output: 74 new work folders from 18 fellows · 50 teach a topic
top subjects: AI for product managers 12 · testing & metrics 10 · how AI models work 9
vs last week: 26 pull requests (30) · 95 frictional logs (72)

beats.role_note: BLUF -- hesitant writer corrects the misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the week in one line. You might expect a pile of status updates. But most new folders are lessons: fifty of seventy-four teach a topic.

props.text: This week's new folders were mostly status updates.

beats.role_note: 74 new work folders as a grid of squares, coloured by kind; dated strip
beats.narration_text: Start with the folders. Seventy-four new work folders landed, from eighteen fellows. By my rough sort, fifty are STEM explainer videos, twenty-three are progress videos, and one is an hours log. Twenty-eight are dated this week. Forty-five are older work, filed this week.

beats.role_note: the 50 topic videos by subject (rough keyword sort), bar chart
beats.narration_text: So what did they teach? I sorted the fifty topic videos by subject. Twelve teach AI to product managers: one fellow's full series. Ten are about testing and metrics, from six different fellows. Nine explain how AI models work. Eight are about making videos with AI. Five cover software and data tools, and the last six are marketing and other topics.

beats.role_note: six real titles dated this week, as cards with folder name + subject
beats.narration_text: A few of the titles. Mixture of Experts. Goodhart's Law: when the proxy stops being the target. Integration Hell. Likely False, Likely True. RAG Explained for Product Managers. And Be the Sentence, about getting quoted by AI search.

beats.role_note: ONE comparison with last week (same script, same definitions)
beats.narration_text: One comparison with last week, counted by the same script. Merged pull requests went from thirty to twenty-six. New work folders, from eighty-four to seventy-four. Fellows with new folders, from twenty-two to eighteen. But frictional logs went up, from seventy-two to ninety-five.

beats.role_note: Boopesh's own two videos last week; delivered for review; GitHub PR pending (honest)
beats.narration_text: And my part. Last week I made two videos. One Week of Fellows, a progress update, runs two twenty-four. The ninety-nine point nine percent Accuracy Trap, on AI fraud detection, runs two twenty-three. Each has a Short, and all four are 4K, delivered for review. My GitHub pull request is still pending: my fork attempt failed, so my folder isn't on main yet, and isn't in these counts.

beats.role_note: the concrete takeaway: turn a week of work into one lesson
beats.narration_text: So here's the takeaway. Your weekly update can teach, too. Take one idea from your week, show one worked example, and say where it breaks. That's a lesson, not just a status report.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF -- prompt read aloud and explained
beats.narration_text: Your turn. With your own project open, paste this into Claude. Find the one idea from my work this week that a newcomer would find hardest, and outline a two-minute explainer: the idea, one worked example, and where it breaks. A good answer points to the files where the idea shows up.
